0.content: Gaming's father, a tea merchant of Qiaoying Village whose family had grown tea for generations before he turned to selling leaves. He wanted Gaming to inherit the business and saw Wushou Dance as a road to poverty and injury. After his wife's death the two drifted apart; when Gaming was hurt yet again, Tak gave away all his son's equipment except the beast head his wife had made, and Gaming left home the next day. Tak secretly asked Communications Office contacts to look out for him and had the assistant Leong write festive letters, but would not swallow his pride. He blamed himself for his wife's illness and dreaded anything happening to their only son; in 4.4 he confided his worries about Gaming's dangerous, unstable life to Zhongli. After watching Gaming's Lantern Rite performance he dropped his opposition and called him a great kid; Gaming hugged him.

1.comment: Gaming: Gaming's mother and her letter
1.content: His unnamed mother married into Qiaoying Village from afar and helped build the tea business. Gaming followed her everywhere as a child and took her speech, her love of dim sum, herbal teas and greens. She supported his Wushou Dance and made his beast head. She died of illness. Her only letter to him, which he keeps folded in a book under his pillow, asks him not to quarrel with his father ("more bark than bite"), to be careful and dress warmly, to keep his promises, to treat true friends sincerely, and not to bottle up his feelings. She told him he was better than char siu after all. The book was her teacup coaster; he admits she never read it either.

2.content: A small red suanni, a young member of the solitary Illuminated Beasts of Chenyu Vale's mountains. Gaming sought a real suanni at Mt. Lingmeng for Wushou inspiration, brought his beast head and a bag of offerings, and was surprised and delighted to find a cute tiny creature on a rock. When he tried to pat it, it attacked him like a living flame, and Gaming instinctively danced against it with his beast head until dusk, copying its moves. It accepted him, and the troupe was founded that day. Man Chai has followed him since.

3.content: Gaming once shared his provisions with a stranger resting by a lake and told her she seemed a wise elder more worthy of respect than the adepti. She was the adeptus Cloud Retainer (he knew she was an adeptus; she now lives in Liyue Harbor as Xianyun), and she was so pleased she resolved to look out for him. In 4.4 she learned of his rift with his father and planned a reconciliation: she had Charlotte buy Tak's tea for Fontaine, sent father and son on the escort, had Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver stage a bandit attack, and used adeptal wind to make his Lantern Rite performance spectacular. He calls her "Aunty Xianyun"; she remade his worn beast head (after he talked her down from ten new giant ones).

4.comment: Gaming: The Mighty Mythical Beasts and Wushou Dance
4.content: Wushou Dance is a Chenyu Vale folk art in which dancers in a beast head and blanket portray a suanni, to drums and cymbals, sometimes on high Plum Blossom Poles. In Liyue Harbor it is a newish curiosity, less beloved than Liyue opera. Gaming founded the Mighty Mythical Beasts after meeting Man Chai and is its head; the wiki also lists Dip Yeuk, a Yilong Wharf local, as a member. His goal is to make Wushou Dance a regular sight in Liyue Harbor, then to bring it to all of Teyvat. Equipment wears out quickly and costs a lot.

key: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency
5.comment: Gaming: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency
5.content: An escort agency based in Yilong Wharf, a sub-organisation of the Communications Office, whose guards protect merchants' cargo and travellers on Liyue's roads. Gaming is its "Gold-Standard Guard", the one who can keep clients happy and beat brigands. Zhigui works there. Longzhou of the Communications Office assigns him jobs from Liyue Harbor.
